definitions.explanation: A person who owns land. Historically refers to wealthy landowners who leased land to tenant farmers. In modern usage, refers to anyone who owns real property.

examples.japanese: {地主|じぬし}に{許可|きょか}をもらう。
examples.english: To get permission from the landowner.

examples.japanese: {地主|じぬし}と{借地人|しゃくちにん}の{間|あいだ}でトラブルが{起|お}きた。
examples.english: A dispute arose between the landowner and the tenant.

examples.japanese: {戦前|せんぜん}の{日本|にほん}では{大|おお}{地主|じぬし}が{広大|こうだい}な{農地|のうち}を{所有|しょゆう}していた。
examples.english: In prewar Japan, large landowners possessed vast farmland.

notes:
HISTORY:
The {地主|じぬし} system was central to pre-modern Japanese agriculture. Large landowners leased rice paddies to tenant farmers ({小作人|こさくにん}), who paid rent in rice. After World War II, the Allied occupation carried out land reform ({農地|のうち}{改革|かいかく}), breaking up large estates and distributing land to tenant farmers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大|おお}{地主|じぬし}: large landowner
- {地主|じぬし}と{小作人|こさくにん}: landowner and tenant farmer
- {不在|ふざい}{地主|じぬし}: absentee landlord
